59938002.s: Wadi Al Malad Dam is near the city of Al Baha and the historic village of Al Malad. The valley has fresh flowing water, a variety of trees and is close to archaeological sites, making it a good place for outings and enjoying nature, especially after the rainy seasons when its lake fills.

59937953.s: Cloud Walk is in Raghdan Forest in Al Baha Region. It features a suspension bridge stretching between two peaks over a deep valley, where visitors walk among the mist and clouds with stunning views of the Sarawat mountains and the valleys of Tihamah. It is a special experience for adventure lovers, and visiting during the day is recommended to enjoy walking among the clouds.

59937888.s: King Fahd Pass Viewpoint is in Raghdan Forest in Al Baha Region and is one of the most beautiful viewpoints in the area. It overlooks the bends of the King Fahd Pass, which links the Sarawat with Tihamah, and its deep valleys. It is known for the thick mist that often fills the place and for its beautiful views at sunset.

59937829.s: Khairah Forest is a forest in Al Baha Region, Saudi Arabia. It is known for the heavy rain that falls on its slopes and foothills in winter and spring, which has given it a wealth of wildlife and plants. It is also often misty and cool throughout the year.

59937828.s: Raghadan is one of the villages of Al Baha Region. It lies north-west of the city of Al Baha, about 4 km away on the main road between Al Baha and Taif, with the village of Al Zarqa between it and the city. It is an intermediary among a group of villages and is known for its forest, one of the most beautiful and best-known forests in the Kingdom. It is the seat of the Bani Khuthaim tribal leadership. In the past Raghadan was famous for its long-established Sunday Souq, held weekly and one of the best-known markets in the region, which drew people from all over.

59937826.s: Raghadan Forest is the forest that distinguishes Al Baha and the southern region, for the density of its trees and its greenery. Its climate is mild throughout the summer. It lies west of Al Baha Region and overlooks the Tihamah region and the King Fahd Pass in Al Baha. Mist climbs the high Sarawat mountains into the forest, especially in the early morning and in the afternoon and well into the night, so the atmosphere here in summer ranges between mild and rainy winter.
59937826.b:
Raghadan Forest is the forest that distinguishes Al Baha and the southern region, for the density of its trees and its greenery. Its climate is mild throughout the summer. It lies west of Al Baha Region and overlooks the Tihamah region and the King Fahd Pass in Al Baha. Mist climbs the high Sarawat mountains into the forest, especially in the early morning and in the afternoon and well into the night, so the atmosphere here in summer ranges between mild and rainy winter.

Adding to the enjoyment of the forest, besides its great height, are its many viewpoints over the depths of Tihamah and its deep valleys, into which the King Fahd Pass descends as one of the important arteries of the region linking its Sarawat highlands with its Tihamah lowlands. The density of the vegetation is another dimension of the forest's beauty, with juniper and talh (acacia) trees and some small shrubs, shade by day and a gentle breeze at night.
59937826.a: 4657 Al Hakam, Al Zaroqi, Al Baha

59937823.s: Al Qeem Park has distinctive green lawns with terraces and lakes, a play corner for children and people of determination, and a lovely walkway. The park also has several kiosks selling food and drinks, as well as tables for productive families.

59937759.s: Wadi Al Aqiq Dam lies south of Al Aqiq Governorate and is the largest dam in the region. It holds large amounts of stored water used by the people of Al Baha Region. The dam attracts tourists because of its location amid forests and dense trees, and visitors come to enjoy its wonderful atmosphere and beautiful natural scenery.

59937725.s: Wadi Tharad Dam is one of the dams in Al Aqiq Governorate, Al Baha Region. It was built to support the region's water supply, and a lake gathers behind it, giving the place a quiet natural character. This makes it a good place for outings and relaxing in nature, especially after the rainy seasons.

59896171.s: The heritage town of Sadus, north-west of the city of Riyadh, is one of the important heritage sites in Riyadh Region. It played a role in the history of the Kingdom and the epic of its unification.

59896168.s: Al Yamamah Martyrs Cemetery is in Al Jubaylah in northern Riyadh. Some of the Companions were buried here after the battle against Musaylimah the Liar in the Wars of Apostasy, among them Zayd ibn al-Khattab, Al-Tufayl ibn Amr, Abu Dujana and Abu Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with them.

59896081.s: The Museum of Past Years takes you on a journey back through time, immerses you in a historical atmosphere, and shows you everything old that the grandfathers lived with.

59896080.s: Diriyah lies on the edge of Riyadh on the banks of Wadi Hanifah. It is notable for its archaeological architectural style and its arched mud walls, which history has made one of the most important centres of culture and trade in the Kingdom. Among its most prominent landmarks is the At-Turaif district, which holds its most important forts and buildings and was the seat of government of the First Saudi State.

59896075.s: Alqa Heritage Village is an ancient heritage village north-west of the city of Al Zulfi, near the Nafud Al Thuwayrat desert and Mount Tuwaiq.
59896075.b:
Alqa Heritage Village is an ancient heritage village north-west of the city of Al Zulfi, near the Nafud Al Thuwayrat desert and Mount Tuwaiq.

The walls of "Alqa town" and its old settlements are among the most important tourist attractions in Al Zulfi, with the remains of forts, houses and old decorated mud buildings.

59896074.s: The Al Duwaihi Museum in Al Zulfi Governorate, one of the governorates of Riyadh Region, holds thousands of archaeological pieces that tell the history of the region, making it one of the most important tourist attractions there.

59896071.s: An old heritage village famous for its water springs, the best known of which are Al Ras, Ain Umm Burj, Ain Umm Hayb and Ain Maliha, which is why it has been densely populated over the ages.

59896061.s: Dar Al-Rahmania stands in the middle of the Al Urayniyah orchard. Its design took into account the surrounding rural environment of Al Ghat, giving it a Najdi character, with mud buildings and Najdi arches, and a mosque whose prayer hall opens onto the courtyard.

59896055.s: The heritage village has the Emirate Palace, an architectural masterpiece built in the Islamic style of architecture, and the historic Mughairan Fort. On the western bank of Wadi Marakh there is a site with many inscriptions and drawings carved on isolated rocks, dating from between 900 BC and 400 AD.

59875672.s: Qaryat al Faw is the archaeological capital of the first Kingdom of Kindah, one of the ancient Sabaean kingdoms. It is one of the most important archaeological sites in the Arabian Peninsula, because it is a complete embodiment of Arab cities before Islam.

59875669.s: Al Sadiriyah Museum is one of the best-known archaeological landmarks in Riyadh Region. It holds more than 30,000 archaeological pieces and old manuscripts from different eras, some dating back more than 3,000 years.

59875665.s: King Abdulaziz's historic palace in Wadi ad-Dawasir is one of the most important landmarks of the governorate. The palace dates from an early stage in the founding of the state, in the reign of King Abdulaziz.
59875665.b: King Abdulaziz's historic palace in Wadi ad-Dawasir is one of the most important landmarks of the governorate. The palace dates from an early stage in the founding of the state, in the reign of King Abdulaziz.

59875652.s: Ushaiqer village expresses the spirit of authenticity and deep heritage, with an architectural art whose charm has not faded or aged over the years. It is surrounded by thick walls, and its winding alleys and narrow passages framed with wood run through hundreds of archaeological mud houses adorned with palm orchards. Together they paint a venerable picture of Najdi architectural design, with its triangular windows and rooftops and its wooden doors, some of which are carved with the names of the families who lived there.

59875649.s: Al Subaie Palace is one of the most prominent historic palaces in Saudi Arabia and is in Shaqra Governorate, Riyadh Region. It was built in the Andalusian Islamic style and stands in the south-western corner of the old town, overlooking the historic markets. King Abdulaziz, may God have mercy on him, used to rest in this palace on his journeys between Riyadh and other regions.
59875649.b:
Al Subaie Palace is one of the most prominent historic palaces in Saudi Arabia and is in Shaqra Governorate, Riyadh Region. It was built in the Andalusian Islamic style and stands in the south-western corner of the old town, overlooking the historic markets. King Abdulaziz, may God have mercy on him, used to rest in this palace on his journeys between Riyadh and other regions.

Al Subaie Palace is more than 80 years old. It was first restored in 1411 AH (1990) and then fully restored in 1421 AH (2000). Al Subaie House reflects the decorations that were common in the central region of the Kingdom. The palace is planned to be turned into a heritage museum, a destination for visitors to discover the rich history of Saudi Arabia and the beauty of its architecture.

59875648.s: Hlewa Market is considered one of the most important heritage markets in Shaqra Governorate in Riyadh Region. It was built in 1350 AH (1931) and consists of a spacious area that gives an accurate picture of Shaqra's special commercial standing in the Arabian Peninsula. It has a group of shops specialising in household goods, textiles, souvenirs and more, as well as a distinctive heritage museum, a library and an outdoor cafe suited to a cup of coffee with family or friends.

59875646.s: Al Halwan Heritage House is an old mud house in the old Deirah of the town of Athaithiyah, part of Marat Governorate in Riyadh Region. It reflects the traditional Najdi architectural style.
